messages:
menna (design): Quick check-in: proposing we replace the floating simulation legend with a slim left rail that can pin to rule groups. Goal: less overlay on long rule text and clearer visual alignment with rules. Thoughts?

joel (pm): Left rail sounds promising. Two concerns: 1) vertical space on 13" laptops, 2) discoverability of reorder handles if we change density.

reka (frontend): We can make the rail collapsible and add a keyboard toggle. For compact lists, show a micro-handle always (small visual) but keep the hit area 32px. On mobile switch to a bottom drawer.

hyejin (a11y): Strong +1 for collapse + keyboard toggle. Requirements: rail must be role="region" with aria-label="simulation legend". Don't rely on color alone to indicate priority 1 use numbers or chevrons too. Also debounce aria-live announcements for simulation status (use ~800ms).

sam (uxwriter): Copy suggestion for compact badges: visual "High" with aria-label="High priority". Tooltip on hover: "High priority 1 runs before lower ones." Keep to <50 chars.

menna (design): Good. UX question: where should inline validation appear during playback? Current mocks use toasts but testers lose them while interacting. I prefer inline under the rule title.

reka (frontend): Inline is better. We'll render a small <div role="status" aria-live="polite"> under each rule when there's a validation. For global results, show a summary toast (aria-atomic) after the run finishes. Debounce live updates to avoid repeated announcements.

hyejin (a11y): Perfect. Also ensure `aria-describedby` links the rule to the validation so screen readers read it when focus lands. When a validation appears but the user is focused elsewhere, do not steal focus.

joel (pm): Drag handle discoverability: tests show hover-only handles get missed. Proposal: in compact mode always-visible subtle handle; in full mode reveal on hover. Also add a keyboard menu with "Move up" / "Move down" actions for accessibility.

sam (uxwriter): Tooltip microcopy: "Drag to reorder rules" or shorter: "Drag to reorder". For the keyboard menu label: "Reorder rule". Keep copy consistent across contexts.

reka (frontend): Implementation detail: we'll add aria-label="Reorder rule" to the handle and a visually-hidden label for screen readers. For touch devices, long-press initiates drag.

hyejin (a11y): Ensure the visually-hidden label is included in the DOM and that the handle is reachable by keyboard (tab). Provide move-up/move-down buttons as an alternative to dragging. Buttons should be small and placed in an overflow menu to keep density.

menna (design): One more: preview legend content. Should we include quick runtime stats (avg latency) and a small playback speed control? Playback speed helps debug ordering/async issues.

joel (pm): I like speed control but keep it minimal: 0.5x/1x/2x. Snapshot button should be prominent in the rail so folks can capture state without hunting. Snapshots must redact any PII by default.

sam (uxwriter): Snapshot confirmation copy: "Snapshot saved" with a secondary link "View". Make toast aria-atomic. If redaction occurs, show brief note: "Sensitive fields redacted".

reka (frontend): Will implement: rail with collapse + keyboard toggle + speed selector + snapshot button. Inline validation under rules with role=status + aria-live polite + 800ms debounce. Micro-handle always visible in compact. Keyboard reorder menu included.

hyejin (a11y): I'll prepare a checklist covering: region roles, aria-labels, aria-describedby for validations, debounce timing, focus behavior when rail toggles (focus moves to first legend item or preview controls), contrast checks (>=4.5), and alternative cues for colorblind users.

menna (design): Action items: Reka = branch `feat/sim-rail` with keyboard tests; Hyejin = a11y checklist; Sam = finalize short strings; Joel = privacy note on snapshot redaction. We'll ship behind a flag and test with power users. Design sync tomorrow to walk the prototype: https://figma.redwood.design/proto/new-rail (comments enabled). :thumbsup:
